subproblem.title: Local uniform continuity of the second derivative of a C^2 function
subproblem.statement: Let E be a real normed space (E : Type with NormedAddCommGroup E and NormedSpace ℝ E) and F : E -> R of class C^2 (ContDiff ℝ 2 F). For every x0 in E and every delta > 0 there is eps > 0 such that, for all x in E with ||x - x0|| <= eps and all Q, Q' in E, |D^2F(x)[Q][Q'] - D^2F(x0)[Q][Q']| <= delta (||Q|| ||Q'||), where D^2F(x)[Q][Q'] = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ F) x Q Q'.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {E : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] (F : E → ℝ), ContDiff ℝ 2 F → ∀ x₀ : E, ∀ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ → ∃ ε : ℝ, 0 < ε ∧ ∀ x : E, ‖x - x₀‖ ≤ ε → ∀ Q Q' : E, |fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ F) x Q Q' - fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ F) x₀ Q Q'| ≤ δ * (‖Q‖ * ‖Q'‖)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Write H(x) := fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ F) x, an element of the normed space E →L[ℝ] (E →L[ℝ] ℝ) of bounded bilinear forms with the operator norm.

1. Continuity of H. F is C^2, so DF = fderiv ℝ F is C^1 (ContDiff.fderiv_right, since 1 + 1 <= 2). Hence its derivative H is continuous (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv, as 1 != 0).

2. Choice of eps. By continuity of H at x0 there is r > 0 with ||H(x) - H(x0)|| < delta whenever dist(x, x0) = ||x - x0|| < r. Put eps := r/2 > 0. If ||x - x0|| <= eps then ||x - x0|| < r, so ||H(x) - H(x0)|| < delta.

3. Bilinear estimate. Let B := H(x) - H(x0). For all Q, Q': B Q Q' = H(x) Q Q' - H(x0) Q Q', since subtraction of continuous linear maps is pointwise (applied twice). Also |B Q Q'| <= ||B|| ||Q|| ||Q'|| (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm₂).

4. Conclusion. For ||x - x0|| <= eps and all Q, Q': |H(x) Q Q' - H(x0) Q Q'| <= ||H(x) - H(x0)|| ||Q|| ||Q'|| <= delta (||Q|| ||Q'||). QED

subproblem.title: Second derivative of a C^2 function along a line
subproblem.statement: Let E be a real normed space (E : Type with NormedAddCommGroup E and NormedSpace ℝ E) and F : E -> R of class C^2 (ContDiff ℝ 2 F). Then for all x, v in E, the real function g(t) = F(x + t v) satisfies deriv (deriv g) 0 = D^2F(x)[v][v], where D^2F(x)[v][v] = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ F) x v v.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ {E : Type} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E] (F : E → ℝ), ContDiff ℝ 2 F → ∀ x v : E, deriv (deriv (fun t : ℝ => F (x + t • v))) 0 = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ F) x v v

1. Regularity. F is C^2 and 2 != 0, so F is differentiable everywhere. Since 1 + 1 <= 2, the derivative map DF = fderiv ℝ F : E -> (E →L[ℝ] ℝ) is C^1 (ContDiff.fderiv_right), hence differentiable everywhere.

2. The line. gamma(t) := x + t v satisfies gamma'(t) = v for every t in R.

3. First derivative of g. By the chain rule, for every t, g has derivative DF(x + t v)[v] = fderiv ℝ F (x + t v) v at t. So the function deriv g equals t -> fderiv ℝ F (x + t v) v for all t.

4. Second derivative. By the chain rule again, the curve t -> DF(x + t v) in E →L[ℝ] ℝ has derivative D(DF)(gamma(0))[gamma'(0)] = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ F) x v at t = 0, since gamma(0) = x + 0 v = x. Evaluation at the fixed vector v is a continuous linear map (E →L[ℝ] ℝ) -> R. Equivalently, apply the product rule to the pairing of this operator-valued curve with the constant curve v, whose derivative is 0. Hence t -> DF(x + t v) v has derivative (fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ F) x v) v at 0.

5. Conclusion. By steps 3 and 4, deriv (deriv g) 0 = deriv (t -> fderiv ℝ F (x + t v) v) 0 = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ F) x v v. QED

Put s := sqrt(sum_a ||Q e_a||^2) >= 0.

subproblem.natural_proof:
Notation: fix n, l, Q. L := Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ, J is the area integrand, and S := G(Q) is the n x n matrix S_{ab} = <Q e_a, Q e_b>.

1. J is C^2. By the sibling integrand_smooth (Submission.dohr_eb_ail_contDiff), J is C^infinity on L, hence C^2 (2 <= infinity).

2. Reduction to a line. Apply the sibling line_second_deriv (Submission.dohr_eb_ail_line_second_deriv) with E = L, F = J, x = 0, v = Q: fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ J) 0 Q Q = deriv (deriv (t -> J(0 + t Q))) 0.

3. Scaling of the Gram matrix. For t in R and a in Fin n, (0 + t Q) e_a = t (Q e_a). So G(0 + t Q)_{ab} = <t Q e_a, t Q e_b> = t^2 <Q e_a, Q e_b> = (t^2 S)_{ab}. Hence J(0 + t Q) = sqrt(det(I + t^2 S)) for every t, i.e. the two functions of t are equal.

4. One-variable computation. By the sibling sqrt_det_second_deriv (Submission.dohr_eb_ail_sqrt_det_second_deriv) applied to S: deriv (deriv (t -> sqrt(det(I + t^2 S)))) 0 = trace S.

5. Trace. trace S = sum_a S_{aa} = sum_a <Q e_a, Q e_a> = sum_a ||Q e_a||^2.

Combining steps 2-5: fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ J) 0 Q Q = sum_a ||Q e_a||^2. QED
